Description & Requirements

About Bloomberg:

Bloomberg is a leading provider of financial data, news, and analytics, serving the world's financial community through the Bloomberg Terminal, a powerful platform that connects decision-makers to a dynamic network of information, people, and ideas.

The Bloomberg CTO Office is the future-looking technical product arm of Bloomberg L.P. We envision, design, and prototype the next generation of products that heavily rely on cutting edge technologies. Our projects include machine learning-powered products, generative AI and cloud computing infrastructure and strategy, our desktop and mobile applications, open source stewardship, and more. We partner with all aspects of our company, including financial products, broadcast and media, internal tech, and beyond. We are passionate about what we do.

What's In It For You

We are seeking a strategic and driven Head of Product to own the vision, strategy, product team, partner operating model, and measurable client and commercial outcomes for the Bloomberg Professional App.

This is a high-impact leadership role at a pivotal moment for Bloomberg. As AI reshapes how financial professionals discover information, interact with workflows, and make decisions, you will help define the future role of mobile within the Bloomberg ecosystem.

You will lead the Mobile Product team and work across Product, Design, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to deliver a cohesive, best-in-class mobile experience that extends the power of Bloomberg beyond the desktop.

You will shape how AI-powered experiences come to life on mobile, where speed, focus, context, and trust matter most. You will also ensure the Bloomberg Professional App strengthens the value of the Bloomberg Anywhere offering and delivers clear impact for clients and the business.

We'll trust you to

Lead and Develop the Product Team: Build, manage, and mentor a team of Product Managers spanning mobile platform experience, AI, and partner enablement, setting clear expectations, coaching toward best practices, and cultivating a high-performing product culture.
Define the Mobile Vision and Strategy: Own a multi-year roadmap for Bloomberg Professional mobile (iOS and Android), defining the role of mobile within the broader ecosystem as AI reshapes how financial professionals discover information and make decisions.
Help Define the Long-Term Role of Mobile within the Bloomberg Ecosystem: Develop a perspective on how desktop, mobile, AI assistants, intelligent agents, and emerging interaction models should work together to create differentiated value for Bloomberg clients.
Drive the AI-First Experience: Spearhead the transition to mobile-native AI, ensuring that Bloomberg’s key products and intelligent agents are delivered with high quality, speed, and contextual relevance.
Own Outcomes, Not Features: Define and track engagement, retention, and stickiness KPIs, fostering an outcome-based success criteria. Report impact to senior leadership and use data to drive prioritisation across the portfolio.
Scale the Mobile Ecosystem Model: Establish & Scale the operating model for how distributed product teams integrate into the mobile app. You will ensure a cohesive client experience is maintained while partnering with teams across the business and interfacing with Terminal application frameworks teams to ensure this federated ecosystem is built on a robust, performant, and shared foundation.
Champion Mobile as a Strategic Platform Across the Firm: Act as the senior voice of the client for the Bloomberg Professional mobile experience across the company. Set the agenda for how mobile is represented in firmwide product strategy, partnering with Product, Design, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and Product leaders to align mobile priorities with desktop roadmaps, AI initiatives, and Bloomberg’s highest-priority client and commercial objectives.
Operate as a True Partner with Design and Engineering: Build a strong Product–Design–Engineering partnership, bringing Product, UX, and technical perspectives together early and consistently. Co-own discovery, problem framing, solution design, and delivery to ensure the Bloomberg Professional App reflects deep client understanding, mobile-native craft, and high-quality execution.
Drive Commercial Impact: Ensure the Professional App provides meaningful, measurable, and growing ROI for the business. Partner with Sales to integrate mobile into campaign infrastructure, support retention strategies for low-engagement users, and articulate the Bloomberg Anywhere value proposition to the market.
Govern App Store Presence and Platform Compliance: Own iOS and Android release governance, platform compliance, and proactive OS adoption — ensuring the app meets the security, regulatory, and accessibility standards required of a regulated-industry financial platform.

10+ years of product management experience, including at least 5 years leading product teams and managing other Product Managers
Proven ability to navigate complex, matrixed enterprise environments and align cross-functional leadership, Engineering, UX, Data, Sales, Compliance, behind a shared product direction
Experience leading product organizations through ambiguity, helping define product strategy during periods of technological and organizational change
Strong understanding of mobile platforms across iOS and Android, with the technical depth to partner credibly with engineering leads on platform architecture, APIs, and shared services
Significant experience delivering mobile products in financial services, fintech, market data or a comparable regulated, real-time environment
Demonstrated success defining and tracking product metrics that tie to business outcomes, engagement, retention, adoption, commercial impact
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence at senior levels and operate in a fast-paced, high-visibility environment
Bachelor's degree or higher in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Product Management, Finance, Business)

Broad fluency in financial markets, instruments and professional workflows, ideally direct familiarity with the Bloomberg Terminal
Experience with generative AI, conversational interfaces or LLM-enabled product surfaces, particularly on mobile
A track record of translating feature-dense desktop products into focused, mobile-native experiences
Experience managing large, federated application ecosystems, including App Store governance, partner enablement and framework-driven development at scale
Proficiency with AI productivity and prototyping tools, with the ability to use them to accelerate product discovery, prototype concepts and partner more effectively with Engineering
Background working with newsroom, real-time content or communications product teams
A demonstrable obsession with mobile craft: glanceable design, push and alerting strategy, contextual intelligence and the user journeys that earn a place on a professional's home screen

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (Marketplace)
jobs.description:
About Traba

Traba is building the AI operating layer for the light industrial supply chain.

We started in the workforce space because contingent labor is the biggest operational pain point our manufacturing and logistics customers face. We used it to embed ourselves inside their daily operations and create a far better customer experience through technology. Now those same customers are pulling us beyond staffing into the broader operational workflows that run their facilities. That foundation gave us proprietary data from millions of shifts and deep enterprise relationships.

But our edge is more than data. By connecting to the systems running across every facility and activating the workers already on our platform to execute against them, we are building applied AI that drives real productivity gains and transforms how the global supply chain operates at scale.

We are backed by Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst.

The Role

The product is the labor itself: the workers we match and deploy into warehouses and manufacturing facilities across the country (and eventually, the world). Every product decision impacts supply, demand, fulfillment, customer outcomes, and marketplace health.

We are looking for an entrepreneurial and experienced Product Manager to own and evolve our staffing product that sits at the center of Traba’s marketplace. You'll own the staffing product at the center of Traba's marketplace, working across both sides: the enterprise customers who run distribution centers and manufacturing lines, and the workers whose trust and reliability are what those customers are actually buying.

In addition to collaborating with software engineers, product designers, data analysts, and other product managers on the team, you’ll also work closely with our operations and field teams to design, build, and ship practical solutions into industrial facilities.

This role reports directly to our VP of Product.

What You’ll Do

Architect and steward our product strategy across critical staffing and marketplace workflows
Solve complex marketplace problems by balancing customer needs, operational realities, and business outcomes
Write detailed product requirements and partner closely with engineering teams to execute solutions
Build systems that improve marketplace liquidity, fulfillment, matching quality, and operational efficiency
Use data to uncover hidden patterns and answer critical marketplace and customer questions
Translate operational complexity into scalable product systems
Scale operations by designing smart internal tooling and technical solutions
Launch and iterate products across customers, regions, and operational environments
Visualize and communicate complex ideas from systems and workflows to operational models and product strategy
Socialize your work across all levels and departments while synthesizing diverse stakeholder feedback

What We’re Looking For

Customer-obsessed.
Product judgment is downstream of customer truth, and you act like it. You spend time on-site with the people using your product, on both sides of the marketplace. When the team debates a decision, you're the one who's already talked to three customers and two workers about it.

AI-native operator.
You've changed how you work because of AI, not just added it to your stack. You prototype before writing a spec. You check in code to the production repo. You build internal agents to do research and analysis that used to take days. This shows up in how you operate, not how you describe yourself.

Marketplace operator.
You have deep experience building products in two-sided marketplaces where supply and demand dynamics are real and operational complexity matters. You understand marketplace liquidity, matching systems, incentives, fulfillment, trust, and the tradeoffs required to maintain marketplace health at scale.

Enterprise B2B muscle.
You have built products for complex customers with multiple stakeholders, long sales cycles, and operational rollout challenges. You are comfortable navigating environments with regional operators, warehouse leadership, procurement processes, and layered customer organizations.

First-principles thinker.
You spend equal time thinking about why, how, and what. You understand that strong product judgment often comes from deeply understanding systems and constraints rather than applying generic playbooks.

Operations systems builder.
You have built operational products or internal tools that powered real businesses. You understand workflows deeply and know how to create leverage through systems that help teams operate more efficiently.

Builder mentality.
Inventive and scrappy problem solver. You move quickly, embrace ambiguity, and know how to create meaningful outcomes without relying on giant teams or excessive process.

Deeply collaborative.
You work seamlessly across product, design, engineering, data, operations, sales, customer teams, and leadership. You know how to align stakeholders and build trust across functions.

What You’ll Bring

5 - 7 years of experience as a Product Manager
Evidence of shipping products that materially moved business outcomes
Strong experience in two-sided marketplaces with real supply and demand dynamics
Experience building enterprise products with multi-stakeholder customers and complex operational environments
Experience building internal operational tooling or systems that supported real business execution
Strong technical fluency and ability to work deeply with engineering teams
Experience operating in startup environments where speed and ownership matter
Desire to work at a startup and cover an exceptionally wide surface area
A strong work ethic and desire to build a category-defining company

Benefits

📈 Start-up equity
💰 Competitive Salary
🩺 100% Paid health, dental & vision coverage
🍽️ Dinner Provided via Grubhub & stocked kitchen for NY employees
🚍 Commuter benefit
🎤 Team building events
🏋🏽 Gympass Benefit

✚✚ Additional: One Medical Membership, Gympass, HSA via Optum, Talkspace, Health Advocate, Teledoc Health

The compensation range for this position is set between $180,000 and $210,000, reflecting our market analysis and other relevant considerations. However, exceptions may be made for candidates with qualifications that significantly differ from those outlined in the job description.We also offer a highly competitive equity package designed to ensure you share meaningfully in the long-term success and upside of the business.

The position is based onsite in New York City or San Francisco, five days per week, giving you the opportunity to collaborate closely with a high-performing team in a fast-paced, energetic environment. We are on a path to change the world for the better. We create and communicate a bold direction that inspires a life-changing vision. We don’t sacrifice long-term value for short-term results.

Olympian’s Work Ethic -
Changing the world never comes easy. We work harder, longer, and smarter, not just two out of three. We put everything we have on the field.

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho — New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What You'd Actually Own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who This Is For

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale.
Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You Are The Kind Of Person Who

Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.
Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.
Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."
Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.
Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.
Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."
Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who This Is NOT For

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior.
This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's Also Probably Not Your Fit If

Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.
Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.
Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.
You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.
You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.
"Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.
You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

How We Work

Small pods. Artifact first. Designers own their surfaces end to end, including research, QA, and the fight to get it shipped right. We use AI natively and expect you to. The design team is heads down on building the governed frontend layer this quarter, and this role is central to it.

We're in the office in New York because the best systems work happens shoulder to shoulder, obsessing over a real screen.

The bar

Restraint over decoration. Confidence over noise. Interfaces that feel calm because someone sweated every detail so the user never has to, and that feel alive because the motion is considered, not bolted on. We care about how money moving feels, how a card creation confirms, how a state transition lands. If "it looks fun, but does it do anything" is a question you ask yourself unprompted, you'll fit right in.

How To Apply

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd architect our token layer, we should talk.

Come ready to do two things when we meet, walk us through a real, working file (not just the polished case study frames), and show us a design system you actually built and governed. Bring one deeply complex, systems level project and one piece you're proud of at the pixel level, and tell us plainly which decisions were yours.

THE ROLE

We're seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the modernization of an established, market-leading compliance product with a large, loyal customer base and a long heritage in the mortgage lending space.

This is not a maintenance role, and it is not a Product Owner role. We are hiring a strategic product leader to answer the hard questions first — what the modern product should be, which capabilities carry forward, which workflows get reimagined, and how we migrate thousands of customers without breaking their trust — and then drive that vision through delivery. You'll be handed a product with real revenue, real customers, and real technical debt, and asked to chart its next decade.

You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy. You will set the strategy, build the business case, define the roadmap, and make the calls — with support from leadership, but without someone handing you a prioritized backlog. The right candidate finds ambiguity energizing: you know how to go deep with customers, size markets, pressure-test assumptions with Engineering, and turn an open-ended mandate into a sequenced plan the whole company can rally behind.

Rho — New York (in person)

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What You'd Actually Own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who This Is For

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale.
Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You Are The Kind Of Person Who

Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.
Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.
Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."
Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.
Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.
Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."
Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who This Is NOT For

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior.
This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's Also Probably Not Your Fit If

Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.
Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.
Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.
You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.
You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.
"Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.
You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, Ncontracts leads the industry in integrated risk management and compliance solutions, serving over 5,000 financial institutions nationwide. THE ROLE

We're seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the modernization of an established, market-leading compliance product with a large, loyal customer base and a long heritage in the mortgage lending space.

This is not a maintenance role, and it is not a Product Owner role. We are hiring a strategic product leader to answer the hard questions first — what the modern product should be, which capabilities carry forward, which workflows get reimagined, and how we migrate thousands of customers without breaking their trust — and then drive that vision through delivery. You'll be handed a product with real revenue, real customers, and real technical debt, and asked to chart its next decade.

You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy. You will set the strategy, build the business case, define the roadmap, and make the calls — with support from leadership, but without someone handing you a prioritized backlog. The right candidate finds ambiguity energizing: you know how to go deep with customers, size markets, pressure-test assumptions with Engineering, and turn an open-ended mandate into a sequenced plan the whole company can rally behind.

As we continue evolving our lending compliance portfolio toward a more integrated, AI-enabled platform, this role sits at the center of one of the most consequential product bets we're making.

YOU WILL

Product Strategy & Vision (50%)

Own the end-to-end modernization strategy for a legacy product line: define the target-state product, the migration path, and the sequencing of investment across a multi-year horizon

Build and defend the business case — market sizing, retention risk, expansion opportunity, and build/buy/partner trade-offs — with executive leadership
Define what carries forward, what gets reimagined, and what gets sunset, and own the communication of those decisions internally and externally
Evaluate where AI-native capabilities should replace legacy workflows rather than merely re-skinning them

Delivery Leadership (30%)

A Communicator: You can articulate a multi-year vision to executives, a sprint's trade-offs to engineers, and a migration plan to a nervous 20-year customer — and be credible with all three.

Company Description
CHIME is a social media agency that partners with bold brands to create content that connects, converts, and stands out in crowded digital spaces. The team builds end-to-end digital strategies, from high-level planning to storytelling and execution tailored to each platform. CHIME focuses on strategy, content creation, community engagement, and sustainable growth rather than short-lived trends. The agency’s goal is to make brand feeds distinctive, memorable, and impossible to ignore. Applicants will join a culture that values creativity, smart experimentation, and measurable impact.
Role Description
The Vice President of Product Strategy is a full-time, remote role responsible for defining and driving CHIME’s product vision across services, tools, and digital offerings. This leader will oversee product strategy, roadmapping, and portfolio management, ensuring alignment with business objectives and market opportunities. Day-to-day responsibilities include analyzing customer needs and market data, guiding product discovery, and collaborating with cross-functional partners in marketing, operations, creative, and technology. The role will involve prioritizing initiatives, setting measurable goals, and leading product teams to deliver scalable, differentiated solutions for clients. The Vice President will also manage budgets and performance metrics for the product portfolio and present insights and recommendations to senior leadership.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong Product Strategy and Strategic Planning skills for defining vision, setting priorities, and aligning roadmaps with business goals.
Candidates should possess solid Product Management capabilities for managing portfolios, overseeing execution, and coordinating cross-functional delivery.
Candidates should possess robust Analytical Skills for interpreting market data, client feedback, performance metrics, and financial outcomes.
Candidates should possess Finance-related skills for budgeting, forecasting, and evaluating product profitability and ROI.
Demonstrated leadership experience in product or strategy roles, preferably within digital, media, SaaS, or marketing-related environments.
Proven ability to work effectively in a remote, distributed team, with clear communication and outcomes-focused collaboration.
Experience bringing new products or services to market, including go-to-market planning and stakeholder alignment.
Advanced degree or equivalent experience in Business, Marketing, Product Management, or a related field is preferred.
